jobs.title: Director, Software Engineering, Agent Platform
jobs.excerpt: Our PurposeAt SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future.
jobs.description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Director, Software Engineering, Agent Platform, you will be tasked with leading the Agent Platform organization, which owns the control plane that every SentinelOne agent depends on: agent communication and configuration, agent management and health, and the detection services that turn agent telemetry into customer protection. When this platform is healthy, the rest of the product works; when it is not, customers feel it immediately. This is a US-based role leading a distributed organization of roughly 45 engineers across four teams in the Czech Republic, Israel, India and the United States, where you will own delivery, operational health and the customer- and executive-facing side of the domain in US business hours, and partner closely with the SaaS Platform architecture group driving the re-architecture of the platform.

This role requires candidates to be based in the EST or CST time zones, given the required overlap with globally distributed engineering teams.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Own the domain end to end, including delivery, operational health, quality and roadmap commitments for the Agent Platform organization.
  • Drive reliability by continuing the reliability program already under way: reduce incident inflow, close corrective actions against a clock, and build the observability that catches problems before customers do.
  • Lead and grow managers: four engineering managers across three geographies report into this role. Develop them, hold a consistent bar, and build leadership depth in the organization.
  • Represent the domain to executives and customers, owning executive communication during incidents and in regular forums, and engaging directly with enterprise, MSSP and federal customers on platform questions.
  • Partner across the platform with the agent and endpoint organizations, the SaaS Platform architecture group, Product Management and SRE to land cross-domain outcomes.
  • Execute the re-architecture: the domain is part-way through moving from a monolithic control plane to a set of regional, horizontally scalable services, and onto a modern container-based deployment model. Own the delivery of that transition for your teams, while keeping the existing platform running for customers throughout.
  • Plan capacity and headcount, balancing reliability, re-architecture and feature delivery, and make the trade-offs explicit to Product and to leadership.
  • Build US presence by growing senior engineering capability in the US alongside the existing teams, so the domain has depth in US hours.
  • Deliver on what success looks like in the first year: incident inflow for the domain is materially lower and the trend is sustained, with corrective actions closing inside the target window rather than accumulating; leadership and customers get a clear, proactive picture of the domain's health, and problems surface from the team before they surface elsewhere; major milestones in the move to scalable, regionally deployed services and the modernisation of the deployment platform are delivered, without regressions visible to customers; the four teams operate predictably against their plans, and the managers are visibly stronger; and US senior engineering presence in the domain has grown.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • Distributed leadership: demonstrated success leading engineering teams across multiple time zones and cultures, with concrete examples of how you made it work rather than worked around it, through clear ownership, strong written communication, deliberate overlap, and trust built without being in the same room.
  • Operational ownership: experience running a high-availability SaaS platform in production, including incident command, root cause discipline, SLOs, and turning a poor reliability trend around with data.
  • Technical depth: a strong background in distributed backend systems at scale, including cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, data stores and multi-tenancy, with the ability to hold a credible technical conversation with staff engineers and architects, and to tell a well-reasoned design from a weak one.
  • Executive and customer communication: the ability to give leadership an accurate picture, including when the accurate version is the worse-sounding one, and to represent engineering credibly in front of customers.
  • Delivery discipline: a track record of predictable execution, with clear ownership, planning that holds, and commitments that land.
  • People leadership: experience managing managers, hiring senior engineers, and raising the bar of an organization you inherited.
  • Business judgement: the ability to connect engineering investment to customer outcomes and to explain the trade-offs between reliability, re-architecture and new capability.
  • Typically 12 or more years in software engineering, with at least 3 years leading multiple teams through managers, in a SaaS or cloud infrastructure environment.
  • Security domain experience, which is an advantage but not required.
  • A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Equity & Rewards

  • Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

Time Off & Wellbeing

  • Flexible time off
  • Paid company holidays and paid sick time
  • Gender-neutral parental leave
  • Grandparent leave

Insurance & Financial Security

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Health and dependent care FSA
  • Voluntary benefits (hospital, accident, critical illness)
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • ARAG pre-paid legal
  • Nationwide pet insurance
  • Cancer Care program
  • Global business travel medical insurance

Work Perks & Flexibility

  • Home office allowance
  • Mobile phone reimbursement

Wellness & Lifestyle

  • Wellness coach
  • Wellness/gym reimbursement
  • Fertility coverage
  • Adoption & surrogacy reimbursement

This U.S. role has a base pay range that will vary based on the location of the candidate. For some locations, a different pay range may apply. If so, this range will be provided to you during the recruiting process. You can also reach out to the recruiter with any questions.

$206,250—$309,000 USD

Vatica Health and Cozeva bring together clinical expertise and technology to support risk adjustment, quality, and value-based care. Our teams help providers and health plans use clinical information to improve documentation and identify care gaps.

As a Clinical Nurse Consultant I, you will use your clinical judgment to turn information from medical records and payer data into clear findings that help providers accurately document member conditions and identify gaps in care. You will work directly with providers and practice teams, combining detailed chart review with relationship building and technology support.

This clinical production role requires independent workload management and consistent performance against chart completion and quality standards. Work is primarily remote, with travel to provider offices for training as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate clinical evidence for active conditions relevant to the applicable risk adjustment model and present findings to support provider condition validation decisions.
  • Reconcile conflicting or incomplete clinical information.
  • Identify open quality-of-care gaps and communicate findings to practice teams for follow-up.
  • Complete chart reviews within established productivity targets and deadlines while meeting quality assurance standards for accuracy and compliance.
  • Build effective relationships with providers and office staff and follow up on outstanding items to meet deadlines.
  • Train and support providers and practice staff on company technology and workflows, including onsite training as needed.
  • Share clinical knowledge and best practices with colleagues to support consistent, accurate chart reviews.

Requirements

  • Active, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license.
  • Minimum of three years of recent RN clinical experience assessing complex patient conditions and interpreting clinical documentation.
  • Demonstrated clinical judgment in evaluating conflicting information and identifying documentation gaps.
  • Clear, professional communication of clinical findings and documentation questions to providers and practice staff.
  • Proficiency with EMRs and web-based applications, including navigating multiple systems and learning new technology independently.
  • Demonstrated success managing detailed clinical work against productivity, accuracy, and deadline expectations.
  • Effective independent workload management and collaboration in a remote team environment.
  • Ability to travel occasionally to local provider offices, with access to a personal vehicle or other reliable transportation.

Preferred Qualifications

As a condition of employment, candidates will be required to complete pre-employment screening including professional reference checks and a criminal record check.

Benefits

Our unwavering commitment to safety and quality drives excellence on every project, every day.

jobs.excerpt: Are you looking for more in life than just building another data pipeline?
jobs.description:
Are you looking for more in life than just building another data pipeline? Does upending cybersecurity resonate with you? We're a rapidly expanding cybersecurity company revolutionizing vulnerability management for organizations of all sizes. For our customers, vulnerability management has historically been a game of catch-up, with fragmented data, limited asset coverage, and manual processes.

Nucleus' primary mission is to create a fast, scalable platform that brings together large volumes of security data and transforms it into actionable insights, making vulnerability management simple, efficient, and effective.

We're looking for a Staff / Principal Data Engineer to help define and evolve the architecture behind our data platform. This is a senior technical leadership role for an engineer who thrives on solving complex data problems at scale, designing systems that process large and growing datasets, and establishing patterns that other engineers can build upon.

What You Will Do

  • Own the architecture and evolution of large-scale data processing and analytics systems, from ingestion and normalization through transformation, aggregation, and customer-facing analytics.

  • Design and evolve data models that support high-volume analytical workloads while balancing query performance, storage efficiency, maintainability, and scalability.

  • Design and optimize complex analytical SQL queries operating across large datasets, identifying performance bottlenecks and developing scalable solutions.

  • Architect distributed and asynchronous job processing systems capable of reliably processing large volumes of data across concurrent workloads.

  • Design and evolve Spark, Flink or similar technologies based data processing workflows for large-scale transformation, enrichment, aggregation, and computation.

  • Drive the effective use of SingleStore/MemSQL, including schema design, indexing and partitioning strategies, query optimization, and workload design.

  • Establish architectural patterns for batch processing, data transformation, job orchestration, failure recovery, idempotency, and reprocessing.

  • Diagnose complex performance and scalability issues across databases, distributed processing systems, application services, and infrastructure.

  • Partner with engineering and product teams to translate ambiguous analytical and data-processing requirements into scalable technical architectures.

  • Define technical standards and reusable patterns for data modeling, data processing, and analytical query development.

  • Provide technical leadership across engineering initiatives, influencing architecture and mentoring engineers while remaining deeply hands-on with implementation.

  • Identify architectural limitations before they become operational problems and lead improvements that increase the scalability, reliability, and performance of the platform.

The Following Skills and Experience Are Key to Succeeding in This Role

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering, data engineering, or data platform experience, with significant experience designing and operating production data systems.

  • Deep expertise in relational and analytical data modeling, including designing schemas for large-scale analytical and reporting workloads.

  • Expert-level SQL, with demonstrated experience designing, analyzing, and optimizing complex analytical queries over large datasets.

  • Strong experience with SingleStore/MemSQL or comparable distributed SQL/analytical database technologies.

  • Significant hands-on experience with Spark, Flink or similar technologies, including designing and optimizing distributed data-processing workloads.

  • Strong understanding of distributed data processing, including partitioning, parallelism, data skew, resource utilization, and performance optimization.

  • Experience designing high-throughput job processing systems, including scheduling, concurrency management, retries, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

  • Experience designing data pipelines that support batch ingestion, transformation, enrichment, aggregation, and downstream analytics.

  • Strong understanding of database performance characteristics, including indexing, partitioning, query execution plans, data distribution, and memory/compute trade-offs.

  • Experience identifying and resolving performance bottlenecks across application, database, and data-processing layers.

  • Proficiency in Python, Java or another production programming language used to build data-processing and distributed systems.

  • Strong understanding of testing strategies for data-intensive systems, including unit, integration, data-quality, and end-to-end testing.

  • Proven ability to independently own technically ambiguous problems and drive them from investigation through production implementation.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence architecture and technical direction across multiple teams without relying solely on organizational authority.

  • Ability to communicate complex data architecture and performance trade-offs clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and technical leadership.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with distributed teams across multiple time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep production experience with SingleStore/MemSQL, particularly with large-scale analytical workloads.

  • Advanced experience with pipeline performance tuning, partitioning strategies, memory management, and optimization of large distributed workloads.

  • Experience designing platforms that support a combination of high-volume ingestion and low-latency analytical queries.

  • Experience building or operating distributed job execution and orchestration systems.

  • Experience with large-scale cybersecurity, vulnerability, asset, telemetry, or event datasets.

  • Experience working with vulnerability scanning technologies across the security stack, including SCA, SAST, DAST, IAST, vulnerability scanning, and container security.

  • Experience designing systems for incremental processing, backfills, replay/reprocessing, deduplication, and late-arriving data.

  • Experience with data observability and operational monitoring for large-scale processing workloads.

  • Experience integrating AI/LLM-driven capabilities with data platforms, including preparing and processing large datasets for AI-assisted analytical workflows.

  • Experience operating data-intensive applications on Linux and cloud infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies in a professional engineering environment.

Why You Should Be Excited

  • Nucleus is a truly unique solution that’s defining a market AND making an actual impact.
  • We’re biased, but you will get to work with one of the best teams in security. We have a lot to get done and we work extremely hard, but we have fun in the process.
  • This role has the opportunity to directly influence how Nucleus approaches data architecture, analytical processing, and scalability as the platform and the datasets it processes continue to grow.
  • Outstanding benefits include flexible PTO, 401k company contribution (not a match, a contribution), generous education and training budget, 100% company-paid healthcare, fully remote work, and more.

Additional Information
At Nucleus we are committed to achieving excellence in our field by combining diversity, collaboration, teamwork, and pride in our work. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability.

Staff Accountant

Reports to: Controller

About the role:

We’re building a smarter, faster accounting function, and you’ll help shape how we get there. As our Staff Accountant, you’ll join a lean, high-performing team reporting to the Controller, where you’ll own key accounting workflows, drive an accurate and timely close, and use AI and automation to make our processes more efficient.

You’ll combine strong accounting fundamentals with a builder’s mindset. We’ll give you the opportunity to strengthen financial controls, improve how work gets done, and grow into more complex areas like multi-entity and technical accounting as our SaaS business scales.

  • Own accounting accuracy. Oversee accounts payable, employee expenses, and procurement workflows in Ramp, using automation to streamline transaction coding, approvals, documentation, and exception tracking.

  • Strengthen reconciliations. Own assigned bank, credit card, and balance sheet reconciliations in NetSuite. Use automated matching and exception detection to focus your time on resolving differences and validating balances.
  • Improve procurement controls. Partner with stakeholders to resolve vendor onboarding, purchasing, approval, and contract renewal exceptions while maintaining accurate records and policy compliance.
  • Maintain accounting integrity. Support fixed asset, depreciation, and lease accounting schedules, ensuring financial records remain accurate and supported.
  • Keep us audit-ready. Maintain clear documentation, validate supporting schedules, and help prepare audit requests, sales tax filings, and annual 1099 reporting.
  • Build smarter workflows. Identify repetitive accounting tasks, test AI-powered solutions, and partner with the team to implement reliable automation with appropriate human review.
  • Turn data into action. Investigate unusual transactions, identify recurring issues, and recommend improvements that strengthen financial accuracy and operational efficiency.

What you bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance and 2+ years of experience in corporate or public accounting.
  • Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP, including accruals, prepaids, fixed assets, and balance sheet reconciliations.

  • AI workflow orchestration skills. You can break a process into clear steps, identify where automation adds value, and apply human review where judgment or financial controls matter.
  • Strong analytical judgment and attention to detail. You investigate discrepancies, challenge assumptions, and take ownership of accurate results.
  • A proactive, collaborative approach. You communicate clearly, raise risks early, and build trust across teams.
  • Curiosity and a drive to improve. You look for better ways to work, adapt quickly, and take pride in delivering reliable results.
  • SaaS or multi-entity accounting experience is a plus.

Why OfficeSpace?

  • High-Performance Culture: At OfficeSpace, we believe in the power of accountability, focus, and drive. Our A-Player team members work together to deliver measurable, meaningful results. We recognize and reward those who push boundaries and achieve excellence.
  • Ownership and Accountability: We trust our employees to take full ownership of their roles, providing the autonomy to innovate and the support to succeed. We seek individuals who are self-motivated and thrive in an environment where they can drive impactful outcomes.
  • Technology-Forward: As a company invested in cutting-edge technology, we integrate AI and other advanced solutions across our platform to enhance productivity, customer experience, and process efficiency. Our team members are excited by the potential of AI and proactively explore ways it can drive our success.
  • Growth Mindset: Continuous learning and improvement are integral to our culture. We encourage our team to embrace challenges, seek knowledge, and develop both personally and professionally.
  • Innovation and Agility: We foster a dynamic, fast-paced environment where fresh ideas and bold solutions are celebrated. We embrace change and thrive on turning challenges into opportunities, with a team that is agile, proactive, and resilient.
  • Collaborative, Results-Driven Environment: We value purposeful collaboration that leads to shared success and stronger results. While our team members are independent, they recognize the value of working together to drive our mission forward.
  • Competitive Benefits and Rewards: OfficeSpace offers comprehensive and competitive benefits packages globally, designed to support our team’s health, well-being, and financial security. We invest in our people so they can excel.

Most senior sales roles come with a fixed product, a territory and a number. This one comes with a portfolio of proven technology, customers who already rely on it, and the freedom to decide what to build next in your region.

The role has two parts:

  • Build. Find the customer problems our technology can solve, shape new propositions with our product and engineering teams, and prove them through demonstrations and pilots.
  • Win. Personally lead and close the deals that turn those propositions into revenue, then make them repeatable.

You will not start from a blank canvas. We are looking for a seasoned enterprise hunter who already knows the buyers in their region and can open doors from day one. As your region grows, so does your remit: you will build the team, partners and plan to take it to the next stage.

Why this role is different

  • Room to create. You are not limited to a price list. Good ideas get product and engineering support, and you will work directly with the CEO and a small leadership team that makes decisions quickly.
  • A strong starting position. Mission-critical software already running inside operators, and a digital experience testing platform used by enterprise engineering teams, give you multiple ways into a customer.
  • Real support. BDR, marketing, pre-sales, solutions and global delivery teams behind you, with operations that are stable and well run.
  • Upside that matches the ambition. Competitive base salary plus variable pay weighted to new business you originate and close.

Our technology portfolio

Our product lines span telecoms service activation and provisioning, SIM and number management, subscriber acquisition and dealer management, customer value management and loyalty, alongside digital experience testing and analytics for mobile, web and streaming applications, including real-device testing, test automation and quality-of-experience analytics.

Together they let you enter a customer through one need, such as activation, loyalty or app quality, and build towards a broader relationship.

Where you will play

  • Telecommunications. Mobile and fixed operators and MVNOs.
  • Banking and financial services. Retail and digital banks, payment providers and fintechs with business-critical digital journeys.
  • Media and entertainment. Broadcasters, streaming and OTT video and audio services.
  • Global technology and digital platforms. Large internet and platform businesses with demanding product and digital experience needs.

Depth in one of these sectors matters more than coverage of all four.

Regions and languages

Asia including China: business-fluent English and Mandarin essential, including leading discovery and negotiation in Mandarin. Other Asian languages advantageous.

Requirements

  • Find the opportunities. Build executive relationships through outreach, industry insight, referrals and partners. Spot unmet needs and buying initiatives before they become tenders.
  • Shape the propositions. With Product, Engineering and Delivery, turn customer insight into offers with a clear use case, pricing, business case and route to market. Test demand and economics before committing resources.
  • Prove them. Run demonstrations, pilots and proofs of concept with agreed success criteria and a clear path to a contract.
  • Close the business. Own complex enterprise pursuits from qualification through procurement, negotiation and signature.
  • Expand and partner. Grow from the first product line into others across the customer, and build a focused group of systems integrators, testing service providers and technology partners with joint target accounts.
  • Build the region. Own the regional plan, pipeline and forecast, and work with Finance on revenue, margin and investment. Recommend and hire the team as demand justifies it.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: senior conversations opened with priority accounts from your existing network, a focused regional plan, agreed targets and a credible qualified pipeline.
  • By six months: first signed business, at least one proposition validated with customers, and evidence of which offers and channels win repeatedly.
  • By twelve months: bookings and revenue on target, multiple new customers, a strong forward pipeline and a plan for the region’s next stage.

What you bring

  • 10+ years of enterprise sales hunting. At least ten years selling B2B technology to large enterprises, with a consistent record of personally originating and closing complex new-logo contracts and beating targets.

  • Ownership. Entrepreneurial, persistent and able to mobilise colleagues who do not report to you. The regional language skills above are essential.

You will stand out if you have founded or launched a business line, built a team, or opened a new market for a technology company.

  • The freedom to shape the market approach and propositions for your region.

jobs.description:
Manager/Assistant Manager – Retail Client Onboarding & KYC (Digital Brokerage & Wealth Management)

Role Overview

The Retail Client Onboarding & KYC officer executes high-throughput, digital-first account opening and verification for individual and wealth management clients. This role balances frictionless customer experience with strict regulatory identity verification, non-face-to-face onboarding compliance, and fraud prevention.

Key Responsibilities

  • Retail Account Opening & Verification: Review and process daily retail account applications submitted via mobile apps and online portals, verifying identity documents, proof of address, and accredited investor documentation.
  • Non-Face-to-Face (NFTF) Compliance: Ensure all digital onboarding aligns strictly with SFC guidelines on non-face-to-face account opening (e.g., designated bank account transfers, certified true copies, e-signatures, and approved biometric e-KYC authentication).
  • Sanctions & PEP Screening: Perform initial automated/manual screening against global sanctions lists, PEP databases, and internal blacklists; escalate suspicious hits to the AML Compliance team.
  • Name & Data Cleansing: Conduct regular data cleansing, maintain client account master data, and update client records (e.g., address changes, tax status shifts, risk tolerance profile updates).
  • Customer Support & Issue Resolution: Liaise with the Customer Service and Retail Sales teams to resolve rejected applications, missing documentation, or deposit-matching exceptions.
  • Workflow & Process Optimization: Partner with product and IT teams to conduct User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for app-based KYC workflow optimizations, automated OCR document recognition, and digital onboarding enhancements.

Key Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or diploma in Finance, Business, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 5-10+ years of experience in retail account opening, client onboarding, or operations within a retail securities brokerage, virtual bank, or digital wealth platform.
  • Familiarity with SFC retail onboarding rules, personal data privacy laws, and anti-fraud controls.
  • High attention to detail with the ability to handle high-volume transaction queues under operational turnaround time (TAT) targets.
  • Tech-savvy with an analytical mindset toward process streamlining.
  • Fluency in Cantonese, English, and Mandarin.

Technology & Operational Efficiency

About MediaRadar

MediaRadar, equips marketing, sales and analytics leaders with the intelligence they need to stay ahead.

Our platform delivers always-on, AI-enabled Creative, Competitive, Commercial and Market

Intelligence—spanning ad strategy, media spend, creative assets and brand messaging across 30+ media

channels and five million brands.

With deep insights into more than 35 million ad and campaign assets and $280 billion in media spend,

MediaRadar provides a single, interoperable source of truth that plugs seamlessly into enterprise

analytics and AI systems. The result: faster, cleaner and more actionable intelligence that drives

competitive advantage.

Job Summary:

As an Associate Manager, Data Operations, you will own the day-to-day performance of a team of Data

Associates across our classification, attribution, and product-catalog workflows. You will sit where human

judgment meets machine learning—turning targets into daily execution, coaching your associates from

task-executors into data-driven critical thinkers, and acting as the first line of defense for quality,

throughput, and SLAs. You will operate within the operating plan set by your Manager, run it relentlessly

on the floor, and surface the insights and improvement ideas that make the plan better.

We are looking for a hands-on operations leader and a force-multiplier for the Manager of Data

Operations.

Requirements

Primary Responsibilities and Impact Drivers: (not limited to)

  • Supervise, coach, and develop a team of 15-20 Data Associates responsible for classification,

attribution, and product catalog management.

  • Monitor and manage team performance against KPIs, including throughput, accuracy, and quality

benchmarks.

  • Serve as the first point of escalation for workflow or process-related issues.
  • Conduct regular quality reviews and provide actionable feedback to ensure data accuracy and

consistency.

  • Identify workflow inefficiencies and partner with managers, automation teams, and governance

specialists to improve processes.

  • Coordinate team scheduling, task assignment, and workload balancing to meet daily and weekly

targets.

  • Ensure compliance with governance standards, documentation, and reporting requirements.
  • Train new hires and ensure associates are up to date on classification guidelines, tools, and

processes.

  • Report team status, coverage, productivity, and quality metrics to management.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively identify and address problems before they escalate, while recognizing opportunities

for efficiency, automation, and quality improvements.

Role Mandate - How you will move the needle

You start your day in your team’s real-time utilization dashboards and queue metrics. You read the data to

anticipate bottlenecks before they form, check the health of in-flight work, and make rapid, high-judgment

calls on how to reallocate associates across queues to protect SLAs.

Through the morning, you are on the floor with your associates. You run quality reviews, give specific,

example-based feedback (what, why, and the rule behind it), and coach your team to do root-cause

analysis on their own defect and throughput data so the same error doesn’t come back twice.

In the afternoon, you connect outward: you partner with Quality, Training, Governance, and your peer

Associate Managers to close process gaps, pilot improvements within your workflows, and feed clear,

evidence-backed recommendations up to your Manager for anything that needs a roadmap-level decision.

You keep the “voice of the client” in view, validating that your team’s output holds up in the real world. You

end the day by reviewing throughput and quality, recognizing your best performers, and making sure your

cross-trained, fungible team is positioned to clear tomorrow’s volume.

Success Measures:

  • Accuracy: Team maintains 98%+ accuracy in ad classification, attribution, and catalog updates.
  • Productivity: Team consistently processes assigned workloads against defined productivity

targets and SLA requirements.

  • Quality Assurance: Less than 2% of team output requires rework due to errors.
  • Team Development: Regular coaching and training lead to measurable improvement in associate

performance.

  • Process Improvement: Implements at least two documented workflow or tool improvements per

quarter.

  • Collaboration: Builds strong working relationships with peers in automation, governance, and

data quality functions.

Short-Term Deliverables (First 90 Days):

  • Baseline your team’s skill sets and identify single points of failure and coverage gaps across the

media types you support.

  • Stand up a rigorous, data-driven feedback loop with your associates using specific defect

examples and root-cause analysis ahead of weekly syncs.

  • Deeply understand your production queues and utilization metrics to optimize the balance

between Core Production (value-add) and Administrative Shrinkage within your team.

Long-Term Deliverables (6 months - 1 year and beyond):

  • Establish a seamless, highly efficient operational flow across time zones that eliminates

geographical friction.

  • Successfully manage the operational integration of new datasets, media channels, or M&A

expansions without linearly increasing headcount.

  • Successfully groom your top Team Leads to be ready for Manager-level responsibilities.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, information systems, or a related field.
  • 4+ years of professional experience in data operations, data quality, content processing, or

shared-services roles.

  • 2+ years directly leading or managing a team, with a proven ability to coach, develop, and hold

people accountable.

  • Demonstrated experience managing high-volume, detail-oriented workflows to tight quality and SLA

standards.

  • Data Fluency: You can use raw data (advanced Excel, PowerBI, Looker) to track performance, spot

bloat, and drive behavioral change in your team.

  • You anticipate challenges, resolve issues fast, and balance daily tactical delivery with a steady

drumbeat of continuous improvement.

  • You actively mentor and elevate associates, guide them through ambiguous operational change,

build actionable growth plans, and cultivate critical thinkers rather than task executors.

  • You treat accuracy as the baseline, not the goal. You uphold and strengthen QA frameworks—even

with legacy tools—so that high-fidelity classification and first-time-right execution are

non-negotiable.

  • (Good to have) Industry Context: Experience in media intelligence, ad-tech, data tagging, taxonomy

management, or content moderation is a strong plus.

The Data Validation Specialist checks that data entering and moving through our systems is accurate, complete, and consistent. The Data Validation Specialist is responsible for labeling, tagging, categorizing, and reviewing large volumes of structured and unstructured data (text, images, audio, video, or multimodal content) according to detailed project guidelines. This role also validates work completed by other annotators, identifies inconsistencies or errors, and provides feedback to improve annotation quality and guideline clarity. The ideal candidate is meticulous, comfortable with repetitive, detail-oriented work, able to follow complex and evolving instructions precisely, and confident flagging ambiguity rather than guessing. As a flex position, the role scales hours up during peak periods such as new AI model launches and down when volume is lower. Assignments are checked to verify progress, through a reporting mechanism by the Artificial Intelligence Project Manager.

What would you do in this role?

DUTIES AND TASKS, including but not limited to the following:


Seeks minimum guidance on the following tasks:

  • Label, tag, transcribe, segment, or categorize data (text, images, video, audio, or sensor data) according to project-specific style guides and taxonomies.
  • Apply bounding boxes, polygons, keypoints, or segmentation masks to visual data as required by computer vision projects.
  • Maintain consistent labeling speed while meeting or exceeding minimum throughput targets without sacrificing accuracy
  • Review annotations completed by peers or vendor teams for accuracy, completeness, and adherence to guidelines.
  • Identify systematic errors, edge cases, and ambiguous instructions; escalate patterns to team leads or guideline owners.
  • Perform spot-checks and full audits on annotated datasets prior to delivery or model training.
  • Track and report quality metrics (accuracy rate, error rate, agreement rate, throughput) using internal tools or spreadsheets.
  • Re-annotate or correct flagged data points and document rationale for changes.
  • Provide structured feedback on annotation guidelines, identifying gaps, contradictions, or unclear edge cases.
  • Participate in calibration sessions to align understanding of labeling standards across the team.
  • Help pilot new annotation tasks, test draft guidelines on sample data, and report findings before full-scale rollout.
  • Document recurring edge cases and contribute examples to internal knowledge bases or FAQs.
  • Work within annotation platforms to complete assigned tasks.
  • Track task assignments, deadlines, and completion status in project management tools.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality and data handling protocols, especially with sensitive, proprietary, or personally identifiable data.
  • Communicate blockers, ambiguous cases, or technical issues promptly to team leads.

QUALIFICATIONS


  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Demonstrated ability to follow detailed written instructions with a high degree of precision.
  • Strong attention to detail and consistency, especially across repetitive tasks performed over long periods.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity, and skilled at flagging uncertain cases rather than guessing.
  • Basic computer literacy: comfortable navigating web-based tools, spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets/Microsoft List), and ticketing/task systems.
  • Strong written communication skills for documenting edge cases and providing feedback.

About the Company

In the coming decades, our world needs far more critical minerals including copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold is the leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.

Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.

KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

jobs.excerpt: Orcrist is building a next generation data intelligence platform using cutting-edge technologies.
jobs.description:
Orcrist is building a next generation data intelligence platform using cutting-edge technologies. We're handling petabyte-scale data with sub-second queries. Our product is a Kubernetes‑based platform delivered as B2B SaaS or as a self‑hosted on‑prem solution, including air‑gapped deployments. We enable customers across defense, law enforcement, and enterprise to turn mission-critical data into actionable intelligence.

Role

Every investigation starts with data. As PM for the Integration team, you make sure analysts in law enforcement and defense have the data they need, when they need it. You own the roadmap for integrating data from commercial vendors, open feeds, social media and messaging platforms, as well as the admin interfaces used to manage these integrations. Your work ensures data arrives current, traceable to its source and ready to use.

This is a largely technical PM role with significant ownership over a platform and admin experience that are still taking shape. You decide what gets built and in what order, working closely with engineers and other product teams to turn provider APIs and data models into scalable integrations and features that support analysts’ investigations. You’ll read API documentation, map provider data to OIP’s data model and write clear, actionable specs that engineers can build from.

What you'll do

  • Own the provider roadmap. We add a source when it answers a question analysts can’t answer today, so you start from the analyst’s problem, not from a provider’s name. You talk regularly with analysts, admins and solutions engineers in law enforcement and defense, and with the upstream teams whose features bring integration requests. You decide which providers come next and what “done” means for each.
  • Write the technical specs. Cover authentication, pagination, rate limits and quotas, incremental sync, deduplication, field mapping, and how failures surface. Every object must carry its provider, fetch time and source URL from the moment it is fetched. Our platform runs as SaaS and on-prem, so you also decide how each source behaves in each distribution.
  • Own the connectors as a product. That covers the contract between connectors and the platform, versioning, and how quickly a new provider goes from evaluation to production. Every connector should make the next one cheaper. Where another team can reach a public source on its own, you give it a safe way to do so instead of putting it in our queue.
  • Own the admin interfaces. That means creating a connection, managing credentials, scheduling, health and status, logs, quota usage and permissions. A source we can’t monitor isn’t delivered, so every live connection needs a health check and clear failure states.
  • Work with partnerships and legal. You collaborate with the Director of OSINT and the Data Acquisition Manager to evaluate vendors, raise licensing and terms-of-service questions before we build, and turn the legal framework (storage, retention, redistribution) into product requirements. You also give the people negotiating contracts technical findings and cost per call.
  • Manage the teams around you. Upstream, you work with the teams building user-facing features, such as graphs and maps, who bring integration requests from their intelligence domain. You help them find the analyst question behind each request and decide whether a shared connector can serve several of them. Downstream, you work with the foundation teams for ontology, machine learning and processing, so incoming data arrives in a shape they can use. You forecast the load of every high-volume source before it goes live.
  • Shape person-focused investigation tools. You own how analysts go from a first lead about a person to a reviewed set of linked online identities. That includes how results are presented and reviewed, and how to avoid paying for the same lookup twice.
  • Measure the integration layer. Track sync success rate, data freshness, time to onboard a provider, active connections, and time to resolve a failed connection.

About you

  • 5+ years as a Product Manager in B2B SaaS, with experience owning a technically complex area end-to-end, such as an integration platform, an API product, or data pipelines.
  • You are comfortable in API documentation. You can discuss OAuth versus API keys, polling versus webhooks, pagination and rate limits with engineers as an equal, and you can try an endpoint yourself in Postman or curl.
  • You have designed admin or configuration interfaces for technical users: connection setup, status and error states, audit trails.
  • You write specs and acceptance criteria that are specific enough to build and test against.
  • You are data-fluent and define quality metrics for reliability and coverage, not just feature delivery.
  • You are comfortable with the legal side of third-party data: licensing, terms of service, GDPR, and provenance requirements.
  • You work well across teams, since integrations touch engineering, partnerships, customer success, and every product that consumes the data.
  • Eligible to work in Germany and willing to travel to Berlin and across DACH for workshops and customer visits.

Nice-to-haves

  • You have built or managed a connector framework, integration marketplace, or iPaaS product.
  • Familiarity with OSINT as a practitioner or product builder, and a sense of where existing collection tools fall short.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment constraints and what they mean for integration architecture.
  • Familiarity with entity resolution or link analysis, and how ingested data feeds them.
  • German language (B1+)
  • Experience working directly with law enforcement or defense users in Germany or the DACH region.

What we offer

  • Real ownership, real impact:Own a critical layer of the platform that every customer relies on. Much of the integration platform and its admin experience is still taking shape, so you identify the problems, set priorities, decide what gets built, and see it through.
  • Remote-first, Germany-wide: Work from wherever you do your best work, with regular team gatherings in Berlin and other off-site locations.
  • Flexibility by default: Flexible working hours help you make work fit your life.
  • Your setup, your way: Get a personal home-office equipment budget to create a workspace that works for you.
  • 30 days of vacation: Take the time you need to recharge and come back with fresh energy.
  • Keep growing: We invest in your personal and professional development.
  • Get rewarded for impact: Performance bonuses are tied to agreed objectives and key results.
  • A warm welcome: Every new team member gets a welcome goodie bag.
  • Good people, good times: From summer and Christmas parties to regular team gatherings, we make time to celebrate together.
  • A mission that matters: Work on challenges with tangible impact on public safety and national security.

jobs.description:
PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here

PATH is a global nonprofit advancing health innovations for the people who need them most. With 50 years of experience, a global team of experts, and trusted partnerships spanning 70+ countries, PATH turns breakthroughs into better health for millions every single year.

Terms of Reference (ToR)


Topic: Assessment on Gonococci associated anti-microbial resistance & self-care among People Living with HIV


Place of Work: New Delhi / Remote


Division: HIV-Hepatitis-STI (HHS)

1. Background


Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the bacterium responsible for gonorrhea, is a growing public health concern due to the emergence and spread of resistance to multiple antibiotics used for treatment. The increasing threat of drug-resistant gonorrhea highlights the need to understand regional resistance patterns, emerging trends, surveillance systems, treatment guidelines, and gaps in research and public health responses.


“Self-care is the ability of individuals, families and communities to promote health, prevent disease, maintain health, and cope with illness and disability with or without the support of a healthcare provider”. The scope of self-care includes (a) health promotion, (b) disease prevention and control, (c) self-medication, (d) providing care to dependent persons, (e) seeking hospital/specialist/primary care if necessary and (f) rehabilitation, including palliative care. World Health Organization (WHO) considering the gap in health care providers work force and the increasing out of pocket expenditure, suggested for innovative health sector response. One of such innovative practice, includes, Self-care.


A comprehensive literature review will be undertaken to synthesize available evidence on gonorrhea-associated AMR in South-East Asia Region and self-care among PLHIV in India. The findings will inform stakeholder discussions and support the identification of evidence gaps, programmatic priorities, and potential areas for strengthening surveillance, research, and response strategies.


2. Objective of the Assignment


  • To explore and understand the prevalence of gonococcal infection, associated antimicrobial resistance and surveillance system in WHO South-East Asian Region.
  • To develop a proposal on self-care among PLHIV, for an integrated self-care model

3. Scope of Work


The consultant will undertake the following activities:


3.1. Conduct a literature review


  • Develop a literature search strategy and identify relevant databases, publications, and other sources of evidence.
  • Review peer-reviewed articles, national reports, surveillance data, treatment guidelines, and publications from relevant public health agencies and international organizations.
  • Examine available evidence on the prevalence and patterns of antimicrobial resistance in N. gonorrhoeae across countries in the region.
  • Review resistance to antibiotics used to treat gonorrhea, including ceftriaxone and other relevant antibiotics.
  • Summarize emerging resistance trends, resistance mechanisms, and relevant research findings.
  • Review existing AMR surveillance systems, laboratory capacity, diagnostic methods, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing practices.
  • Examine national treatment guidelines and public health responses to drug-resistant gonorrhea.
  • Identify gaps in available evidence, surveillance, and research, highlighting differences in data availability across countries.
  • Prepare a draft report presenting the findings, key observations, and recommendations, with appropriate references.

3.2. Presentation of Findings


  • Develop a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the key findings, regional and country-level trends, evidence gaps, and recommendations.
  • Present the findings to the team and/or relevant stakeholders and incorporate initial feedback, as required, in preparation for stakeholder consultation.

3.3. Stakeholder Consultation


  • Preparation of materials for a stakeholder consultation on the literature review findings.
  • Present or support the presentation of key findings during the consultation.
  • Document stakeholder feedback, validate key findings, and capture additional evidence, perspectives, and recommendations emerging from the discussion.

3.4. Finalization of Deliverables


  • Revise the literature review report and PowerPoint presentation based on feedback received during the stakeholder consultation.
  • Submit the final versions of the report and presentation, incorporating agreed changes and ensuring consistency, technical accuracy, and appropriate referencing.

4. Expected Deliverables and Timeline


The assignment will be undertaken over two months, from 1 November to 31 December 2026.Deliverable

Expected timeline

Literature search strategy and review framework

Week 1

Draft literature review report

Weeks 2–3

Draft PowerPoint presentation

Week 4

Stakeholder consultation and documentation of feedback

Weeks 5-6

Final report and revised PowerPoint presentation

Weeks 7-8


The exact consultation date will be agreed with the team.



5. Qualifications and Experience


  • Postgraduate degree (Master’s or PhD) in Microbiology, Basic Sciences, Medical Microbiology, Infectious Diseases, Public Health, Epidemiology, or another relevant discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting literature reviews, evidence synthesis, or scientific research.
  • Familiarity with antimicrobial resistance, preferably antimicrobial resistance in N. gonorrhoeae or other sexually transmitted infections.
  • Strong skills in scientific writing, critical appraisal of research literature, and synthesis of technical evidence.
  • Experience developing technical reports and PowerPoint presentations for scientific or public health audiences.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • Experience engaging with technical experts and public health stakeholders will be an advantage.


6. Duration

The assignment will be for two months (November–December 2026). The consultant will work closely with the designated project team and submit deliverables according to the agreed timeline.



7. Reporting

The consultant will report to the designated project lead or technical focal point. The project team will provide feedback on the draft deliverables and coordinate the stakeholder consultation.



8. Expected Outputs


By the end of the assignment, the consultant will submit:


  • A literature search strategy and evidence review framework.
  • A draft and final literature review report on gonorrhea-associated antimicrobial resistance in the WHO South-East Asia Region.
  • A PowerPoint presentation of the key findings and recommendations revised following stakeholder consultation.

ABOUT ZERO TO THREE

Founded in 1977, ZERO TO THREE works to ensure that babies and toddlers benefit from the early connections that are critical to their well-being and development. SUMMARY

The Content Strategist leads the planning, alignment, and lifecycle management of content for the National Center on Early Development, Teaching and Learning. This role ensures training, technical assistance (TTA), resources, and learning experiences are grounded in evidence, aligned with federal priorities, and useful to Head Start Preschool and Early Head Start programs. A significant portion of this content is developed for publication on HeadStart.gov, requiring a strong focus on clear, accessible, accurate, and timely information for the Head Start community. The Content Strategist connects research and practice, turning complex information into practical resources and ensuring content remains relevant and useful throughout its lifecycle to support high-quality services and improved outcomes for children, families, and staff.

Content Strategy

Ensure content is consistent with Head Start practices and reflects Head Start and other ACF/OHS priorities.

  • Ensure all content is research- and evidence-informed, developmentally appropriate, reflective of best practice and grounded in implementation science.
  • Translate research and policy into clear, actionable guidance for multiple audiences (leaders, teachers, home visitors and TTA providers).
  • Monitor emerging research, policy updates, and field trends to inform content development and updates.

Content Integration

  • Partner with subject matter experts across early learning, other National Centers and contractors, and OHS to ensure cross-disciplinary alignment and coherence.
  • Prevent content silos by identifying overlap, connections, and reinforcement points across topic areas on Headstart.gov and other resource portals supported by OHS.

  • Establish guidelines to ensure content is adult-learning focused, and practice-based.
  • Ensure materials are accessible, scalable, and adaptable across program options and contexts, including urban, rural, and tribal settings.

Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement

  • Work with Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance for content review, revision, and approval.

Collaboration & Leadership

ESSENTIAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, public health, family studies, education, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

This position's salary is estimated to be mid $60,000s to low $80,000s depending on experience, geo-location, budget, and other comparable and similarly scoped internal positions. Also, they may need to remain seated for extended periods, can perform repetitive motions, and reach for objects. An employee is frequently required to hold a writing instrument, communicate verbally, and hear well enough to detect nuances and receive detailed information. They may be required to grasp objects, push, and pull objects, bend, stand, walk, squat, or kneel. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision for data preparation or analysis, and expansive reading.

ESSENTIAL QUALITIES

Depending on work location, the incumbent will typically work indoors in a heated and air-conditioned office, with a mixture of natural, incandescent, and fluorescent light with low to moderate noise levels or be subject to working conditions conducive to a home environment. About the job

The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms.

  • Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout.

  • Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures.

  • Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions.

  • Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock.

  • Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage.

  • Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks.

  • Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations.

  • Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment.

  • Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats.

  • Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus.

  • Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

  • Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles.

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.

  • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones.

About You

You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:

  • Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website.

  • Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms.

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @ or @

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.

What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 6M endpoints and 17M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

Compensation Range: €77,500 to €87,500 base plus bonus and equity

Location: Remote Ireland

What You’ll Do:

Huntress helps protect organizations from cyber threats with a security platform backed by human expertise. The Competitive & Market Intelligence team helps the business understand how buyers make decisions, how competitors and market conditions are changing, and what those changes mean for Huntress.

As the Senior Competitive & Market Intelligence Strategist, you’ll develop deep insight into European buyers, markets, and competitive dynamics while contributing to global CI and MI priorities. You’ll lead research that informs decisions across regions and turn it into practical guidance for Sales, Product, Product Marketing, Marketing, Pricing, and leadership. The role combines strategic research with field engagement, including deal reviews and support for teams across Huntress.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead Europe-focused market and competitive research while contributing to global CMI priorities. Analyze buyer priorities, category and channel dynamics, competitor positioning, pricing and packaging, and differences across regions.

  • Investigate market requirements and differences across regions, with particular depth in European cybersecurity frameworks, regulation, data residency, sovereignty, procurement, and cross-border data access. Build working knowledge of these topics; deep regulatory expertise is not a prerequisite.
  • Support Sales and Sales Engineering with timely competitive guidance across the global field, with Europe as the primary regional focus. Join relevant deal reviews, support active opportunities, and establish recurring CI office hours and team learning sessions. Build practical discovery questions, objection handling, talk tracks, and competitive content sellers can use.
  • Analyze wins, losses, and delayed purchases across regions using buyer interviews and internal evidence, including Salesforce, Gong, and Clozd; while also conduction your own interviews and surveys to distinguish buyer-validated findings from seller-entered data, signals, and inference.
  • Partner with Product Marketing to establish and evolve competitive positioning strategy and messaging, grounded in buyer and market evidence. Turn that strategy into battlecards, competitor comparisons, campaign input, market landscapes, and recommendations for global Sales, Product, Marketing, Pricing, and leadership teams.
  • Partner with global Marketing, PR, and analyst-relations stakeholders on evidence-backed market and competitive context, including media or spokesperson support when appropriate. Use AI tools to accelerate research synthesis and repeatable analysis workflows while validating outputs, protecting sensitive information, and keeping evidence traceable.

Guided by our core values, we strive to create meaningful impact that extends well beyond our bottom line.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please note that all official communication will only come from our verified company email domain @Rippling.com

Who You Are

You are passionate about helping students achieve their educational goals. You thrive in a competitive and collaborative team environment. You are comfortable working remotely and have experience collaborating with others in a virtual environment. You possess a strong attention to detail.

The Vice President of Information Security and Infrastructure reports to the Chief Information Officer and leads ACE’s enterprise cybersecurity, technology risk, infrastructure, and operational resilience efforts. This leader sets the direction for information security and infrastructure, establishes the policies and governance needed to manage risk, and ensures ACE has a secure, reliable, and resilient technology environment. The role advises the CIO, executive leadership, and appropriate Board committees on significant cyber risks, regulatory requirements, major incidents, risk decisions, and technology investments. The Vice President sets clear security expectations, brings the right leaders together to address risk, and ensures significant risks are understood and acted upon. The role balances security and resilience with business needs and cost, while ensuring technology continues to support the College’s growth and strategic priorities.

Compensation

ACE is committed to paying a competitive wage while staying true to our mission of maintaining high quality, affordable programs for our students. The starting salary range for this position is $240,000 plus all full-time employees are eligible for an annual bonus. Offers vary depending on education, prior experience, and expertise being applied to the role.

What We Look for in the Ideal Candidate

  • Executive level communication skills. Must have exceptional communication, organization, and time management skills.
  • Demonstrates self-reliance by meeting/exceeding workflow needs.
  • Demonstrates positive attitude and motivation, concern for students, teamwork, and excellent time management skills.
  • Follows established processes as outlined by organization and leadership.
  • Completes assigned duties based on daily business needs and individual skill set.
  • Consistently produces a high volume of quality work.
  • Capable, adapts as needed, to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.

  • Must support and embrace the College’s Impact mission to improve the people and communities we serve through our civic engagement initiatives.
  • Must have exceptional communication, organization, and time management skills.
  • Must be "self-motivated" as well as creative and efficient in proposing solutions to complex, time-critical problems.
  • Must be collaborative in driving decisions and a team-player.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.
  • Builds and maintains student satisfaction.
  • Recognizes and anticipates student needs.

Day to Day Responsibilities

In this role you will wear different hats, but your skills will be especially essential in the following areas:

  • Partner with the CIO and executive leadership to define and execute multi-year cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud, identity, and operational resilience strategies aligned with ACE’s strategic plan, institutional risk appetite, student experience, growth objectives, and financial priorities.
  • Serve as ACE’s senior executive authority for enterprise cybersecurity risk. Advise the CIO, executive leadership, and appropriate Board committees on material threats, regulatory exposure, control effectiveness, security investments, significant incidents, and risk-treatment decisions.
  • Own the enterprise cybersecurity program and roadmap using NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 or a comparable recognized framework, including current-state and target profiles, maturity objectives, risk-based priorities, funding requirements, accountable owners, and measurable risk-reduction outcomes.
  • Own ACE’s information security governance framework, including policies, standards, control requirements, risk-acceptance criteria, exception management, compliance monitoring, enforcement, annual review, and evidence of control operation.
  • Establish and maintain policies and standards covering acceptable use, identity and access management, data classification and handling, encryption, secure configuration, vulnerability and patch management, logging and monitoring, incident response, third-party risk, cloud security, secure development, business continuity, disaster recovery, artificial intelligence, records retention, and secure disposal.
  • Exercise authority to require remediation of material security weaknesses, approve or reject security exceptions, restrict high-risk technology use, and escalate unresolved or unacceptable risks to the CIO and designated executive governance bodies for formal risk acceptance.
  • Establish clear cybersecurity decision rights, control ownership, accountability, and governance across technology and business functions. Chair or co-chair ACE’s cybersecurity and technology risk governance process as designated by the CIO.
  • Maintain the enterprise cybersecurity risk register and associated remediation portfolio. Translate technical findings into institutional, financial, operational, regulatory, and reputational exposure, with prioritized treatment recommendations and accountable due dates.
  • Direct security operations and incident readiness, including threat monitoring, vulnerability management, identity protection, endpoint and cloud security, incident response, digital forensics coordination, post-incident reviews, and oversight of managed security service providers.
  • Serve as executive incident commander for material cybersecurity events, with authority under approved response plans to activate external partners, isolate systems, suspend affected services, preserve evidence, and coordinate decisions with the CIO, Legal, Privacy, Communications, cyber insurance, and executive leadership.
  • Lead enterprise infrastructure and cloud strategy across Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, networks, endpoints, collaboration platforms, backup, recovery, monitoring, and end-user technology. Ensure architecture is secure, scalable, supportable, resilient, and economically sustainable.
